 Judgment

Though these appeals are listed for admission, they are taken up for final disposal with the consent of learned counsel for both the parties.
2.
Insurer is in appeal in MFA No.103386/2019 challenging the liability saddled on it as well as quantum of compensation.

The claimants are also in appeal in MFA No.105058/2019 praying for enhancement of compensation, not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded under judgment and award dated 30.05.2019 passed in MVC No.924/2018 on the file of learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and Member, MACT-XIII, Hagaribommanahalli (for short, 'Tribunal').
3.

The claimants, who are the parents and siblings of the deceased H. Suresha, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the accidental death of H. Suresha that took place on 13.05.2018 involving Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-35/EC-2209 and Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-22/P-1855.
It is stated that the deceased was aged 24 years and earning Rs.3 lakhs per annum from agriculture and Rs.400 per day from coolie work.
appeared through their counsel and filed separate statement of objections denying the entire claim petition averments.
Respondent No.1 contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of deceased rider of motorcycle in question.
Respondent No.2-Insurance Company contended that driver of offending Tata Indica Car was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
It was contended that the police filed charge sheet against driver-cum-owner of the offending car.
Thus, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. Before the Tribunal, claimant No.1-father of the deceased examined himself as PW1 apart from marking the documents as Exs.P1 to P9.
The respondents did not examine any witness but marked insurance policy as Ex.R1.

The Tribunal based on material on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.21,66,144/- with interest at 8% per annum from the date of judgment till realization on the following heads:
 Loss of dependency Rs.20,16,144/-
 Loss of love and affection Rs. 40,000/-
 Loss of consortium Rs. 80,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

sentences.text: 4 6. While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed monthly income of deceased at Rs.10,000/-, added 40% towards future prospects, applied multiplier of 18 as the deceased was aged 24 years and deducted 1/3rd towards personal expenses of the deceased.

The appellant-Insurer is in appeal before this Court aggrieved by saddling of entire liability on it as well as quantum of compensation, whereas the claimants are also in appeal praying for enhancement of compensation,
not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
7.

Smt. Sharmila M Patil, learned counsel appearing for the appellant-Insurance Company in support of her appeal would contend that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and same needs to be reduced.

Learned counsel further submits that the deceased rider of the motorcycle in question was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident and therefore, contributory negligence has to be fixed on the deceased also.
She would submit that the Tribunal committed an error in deducting 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased instead of 50%, since the deceased was a bachelor.

It is also her submission that interest awarded by the Tribunal on the compensation amount at 8% per annum is on the higher side, since normally on the compensation amount, rate of interest at 6% per annum is awarded.
Thus, she prays for modifying the judgment and award of the Tribunal by allowing the appeal filed by the Insurer.

8. Per contra, Sri. Gurukumar V.A., learned counsel for the appellants/claimants in support of his appeal would strenuously contend that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of driver of the offending Car and as the charge sheet is filed against the driver of offending Car, the Tribunal is justified in saddling entire liability on the driver of offending car in question.

He further submits that the Tribunal committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month, inasmuch as he was earning Rs.3,00,000/- per annum from agriculture and Rs.400/- per day by doing coolie work.
Thus, he prays for allowing the appeal filed by the claimants.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for both the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers along with original records, the only point that would arise for consideration in these appeals is, whether impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal requires interference in the facts and circumstances of the case?
Our answer to the above point would be in the affirmative for the following reasons:
10. The occurrence of the accident on 13.05.2018 involving Motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-35/EC-2209 and Tata Indica Car bearing registration No.KA-22/P-1855 resultant death of deceased H. Suresha is not in dispute in these appeals.
11. It is the contention of the insurance company that rider of the motorcycle i.e. deceased was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

Ex.P3-charge sheet would disclose that the police after investigation filed charge sheet against Driver of offending Tata Indica Car for the offence punishable under Sections 279 and 304-A of IPC and Section 187 of MV Act, but there is no allegation in the charge sheet that rider (deceased) was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

More over, there is also no finding by the Tribunal Hegdala Hanumanthappa @ H. ... vs N.R.Patil @ Ningappa Ramappa Patil @ ... on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72541549/
5 with regard to rider of motorcycle in question was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner.

sentences.text:
12. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh & Others1, at paragraphs-9 has held as follows:
9. If a person, drives a vehicle without a license, he commits an offence.

entities.text: Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh & Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same, by (2008) 12 SCC 436 - 10 - itself, in our opinion, may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.
It has been held by the Courts below that it was the driver of the mini truck who was driving rashly and negligently.
It is one thing to say that the appellant was not possessing any license but no finding of fact has been arrived at that he was driving the two-wheeler rashly and negligently.

If he was not driving rashly and negligently which contributed to the accident, we fail to see as to how, only because he was not having a license, he would be held to be guilty of contributory negligence.
(Underlined by us)

13. A reading of the above paragraph, it is very clear that merely because deceased rider of motorcycle was not having driving license, that itself cannot be held to be guilty of contributory negligence.

Even though the Insurance Company has established the fact of contributory negligence by adducing cogent and acceptable evidence, it cannot escape from its liability to pay compensation on that ground alone.

Non-possession of the driving license by deceased rider of the motorcycle itself, would not be a reason for not granting the award of compensation, if the accident in - 11 - question was on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.

14. The Tribunal on appreciation of entire material on record has proceeded to hold that the accident in question took place due to negligent driving of driver of offending Car and therefore,
saddled entire liability on the insurance company to pay compensation.

Therefore, we find no force in the contention of the insurer regarding fixing of contributory negligence on the part of rider of motorcycle in question i.e. deceased also and accordingly, we reject the same.

15. As regards the quantum of compensation, it is the contention of the claimants that the Tribunal assessed monthly income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- which is on the lower side, since the deceased was earning Rs.3 lakhs per annum from agriculture and Rs.400/- per day by doing coolie work.
But the claimants have not produced any acceptable or cogent evidence on record to prove the avocation and earning of the deceased.

In the absence of any material on record to establish the avocation and earning, this Court and Lok Adalath while settling the Hegdala Hanumanthappa @ H. ... vs N.R.Patil @ Ningappa Ramappa Patil @ ... on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72541549/
6 - 12 - accidental claims of the year 2018, would normally assess the notional income at Rs.11,750/- per month, taking note of the chart prepared by KSLSA based on various factors including the minimum wage fixed.

entities.text: Hegdala Hanumanthappa @ H. ... vs N.R.Patil @ Ningappa Ramappa Patil
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the instant case also, in the absence of any corroborative document to establish the income of the deceased, we are of the opinion that it would be just and appropriate to determine the income of the deceased at Rs.11,750/- p.m. taking note of the income chart prepared by KSLSA and also the minimum wage fixed.
16. The Tribunal has taken the age of the deceased as 24 years, added 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects and adopted multiplier of 18, which in our view is just and proper.
However, the Tribunal erred in deducting 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
It is well settled law that if the deceased is a bachelor, 50% of the assessed income has to be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased.
Accordingly, the claimants would be entitled for - 13 - compensation on the head of loss of dependency at Rs.17,76,600/- (Rs.11,750 + 40/100 x 12 x 18 x 1/2).

17. The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/- towards filial consortium and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, which according to us are just and proper and same is not disturbed.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:
Sl
. No .

Particulars Amount 1. Loss of dependency Rs.17,76,600/-
 (Rs.11,750 + 40/100 x 12 x  18 x 1/2)
2. Loss of estate & Funeral Rs. 30,000/-

 each to parents)
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.18,86,600/- as against Rs.21,66,144/- awarded by the Tribunal.

19. The Tribunal while awarding compensation granted rate of interest at 8% per annum. Taking note of the present rate of Bank interest, we are inclined to - 14 - Hegdala Hanumanthappa @ H. ... vs N.R.Patil @ Ningappa Ramappa Patil @ ... on 15 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72541549/
7 reduce the rate of interest on the compensation amount from 8% awarded by the Tribunal to 6% per annum.

20. In the result, we pass the following:
ORDER a) Both appeals are allowed in part.
b) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.18,86,600/- as against Rs.21,66,144/- awarded by the Tribunal.
c) The entire compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

d) The appellant-Insurer shall deposit the entire compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of six weeks from the - 15 - date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
e) The amount in deposit, if any, be transmitted to the concerned Tribunal forthwith along with original records.
f) The apportionment, deposit and  disbursement shall be made as per the  award of the Tribunal.
g) Registry to transmit the records to the concerned Tribunal forthwith.

h) Draw modified award accordingly.
